name: Repository
why: Several agent runs on one small library, read as a code forge shows them: pull requests with their commits and reviews, issues, discussions and agents, each run's measures side by side, so the runs' setups can be compared issue by issue and a pull request's whole story is one click away.
data: repo.jsonl: one line per record of one run, with `kind` (run, agent, issue, pr, commit, review, comment, merge, close or post), `run` (the run it belongs to), `at` (ISO 8601), `author` (an agent of the run, or for a backlog issue its reporter) and, by kind, `number` (the issue or pull request it belongs to; issues and pull requests share one numbering per run), `title` (of an issue, a pull request, or a discussion's first post), `area` (the part of the library), `closes` (the issue a pull request fixes), `sha` (a commit's id), `verdict` (a review's: approved, changes requested or commented), `reason` (why a close ended its unit without a merge), `thread` (a post's discussion), `team` and `approvals` (a run's size and the approvals a merge needs) and `text` (the body, message, review, comment, post, brief or sign-off note). Records relate through `run` and then `number`, `thread` or `author`; every run works the same backlog, so an issue's number and title match across runs.

accepts.means: the record on line <n>, shown in its pull request, issue, discussion or agent, or a run's brief as that run

declares.means: one run: its measures, with the view narrowed to it
one pull request with its commits, reviews, comments and merge or close
one issue with its comments and the pull requests that close it
one discussion, every post in time order
one agent: its note, its activity and its review partners
